title: Sampling-based metering for prefix/KV cache interactions in interleaved batches
creator: Sara Kim
description:
Problem: current token accounting overcounts or inconsistently attributes cost in flows where requests are served from prefix/KV caches and also participate in coalesced batches. Exact metering for every request is expensive (high cardinality events), produces noisy per-tenant spikes, and complicates rate-limit and quota enforcement.

Goal: introduce a sampling-based metering mode that reduces cardinality, stabilizes per-tenant billing signals, and preserves accurate aggregate billing and quota enforcement within an acceptable error bound. Sampling should handle: full cache hits (prefix only), partial KV hits, interleaved/coalesced batches where some requests are cached and others are not, and retry/redirect scenarios.

Non-goals: change token pricing or billing UX; this is purely a backend measurement technique. This ticket focuses on design and a guarded rollout of sampling and aggregation logic (not billing UI).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end aggregate token accounting error <= 1.5% vs ground-truth for synthetic workloads with mixed cache-hit ratios
Per-customer monthly billing extrapolated from sampling differs <= 2% for customers with >100K tokens/month (larger statistical stability), with documented increased variance for very small customers
Sampling determinism across retries: requests with same request_id should follow the same sampling decision to avoid double-counting during retry flows
Rate limiter preserves correct throttling decisions: sampling does not allow a customer to exceed quota windows (quota enforcement uses conservative counters when needed)
Unit and integration tests covering: pure cache-hit responses, fully uncached responses, partial KV-hit in coalesced batch, retry with idempotent request_id
design_notes:
Approach summary:
1) Per-request deterministic sampling: derive a hash from (tenant_id, request_id, route, timestamp_bucket) to make sampling stable across retries and retries after short redirects. Sampling rate is configurable per-tenant and per-route.
2) For sampled requests, emit full metering events as today (token counts by phase: prompt/response/kv-prefetch). For unsampled requests, emit compact events with only a small set of fields (tenant_id, sampled=false, kv_hit_flags) that the aggregator can use for extrapolation.
3) Aggregator extrapolates token usage by route/tenant/time-bucket using sampled events and counts of compact events. Use stratified buckets by sequence-length class and kv-hit pattern to reduce bias.
4) Quota and rate-limiter integration: primary quota enforcement remains conservative (count all requests that might contribute to token usage) until aggregator confidence for a tenant exceeds a configured threshold. For tenants under confidence threshold, we fall back to full accounting.
5) Edge-case handling: if sampled set misses an unusual pattern (eg. sudden spike in long sequence uncached requests), aggregator triggers an adaptive sampling bump or a fallback full-metering window for that tenant/route.

Trade-offs: sampling lowers event cardinality and storage but introduces statistical noise and complexity in quota enforcement. Deterministic hashing reduces retry double-counting risk but requires coordination of request_id guarantees from the API layer.

Security/Privacy: compact events contain no prompt text or partial outputs; they are limited to flags and small size to avoid exposure of PII in telemetry.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike/prototype): add deterministic sampler in api-gateway to tag requests; emit sampled=true|false flags in request envelope; prototyping only for internal tenants

Phase 2 (metering service): add compact-event ingestion path and aggregator job that extrapolates token counts by tenant/route/time-bucket; implement stratified buckets (seq_len_class x kv_hit_pattern)
Phase 3 (quota integration): implement conservative counters that are updated synchronously for quota-critical tenants; wire sampling config per-tenant in tenant-config service
Phase 4 (feature flag rollout): enable sampling for small set of non-enterprise tenants with monitoring/charts; run A/B validation against full-metering baseline
Phase 5 (gradual ramp): increase tenant coverage, add adaptive bumping logic for anomalous patterns, finalize release notes
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic sampler hash function: collision properties and retry determinism
Integration: compare sampled extrapolated billing vs full accounting using replay of production traces (controlled environment); validate error bounds across cache-hit distributions
Load test: validate compact-event ingestion throughput under peak QPS and storage reduction targets
Chaos test: simulate KV-prefetch spike and verify aggregator adaptive bump fires and initiates temporary full-metering for affected tenant
Quota test: ensure conservative synchronous counters prevent quota-exceeding behavior for tenants with low aggregator confidence
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag. Week 0: internal engineering tenants (10). Week 1-2: opt-in via tenant-config for non-enterprise customers with >10k tokens/day. Create dashboards comparing sampled vs full counts; monitor discrepancy, billing reconciliation, and rate-limit violations. If discrepancy >3% for any tenant, automatically disable sampling and notify SRE + billing. 30-day gradual ramp with rollback capability; enterprise tenants remain on full-metering unless explicitly opted in.
metrics: agg_error_pct (per-tenant, 1h): percent difference between extrapolated tokens and ground-truth from sampled audits
event_cardinality_reduction: ratio of raw metering events vs compact+sampled events
quota_violations: count of quota breaches detected post-sampling vs baseline
adaptive_bump_count: number of times the system escalated tenant to full-metering
cost_storage_reduction: ingestion/storage cost delta for metering pipeline
migration_notes: Backwards-compat: sampled events contain version header. Aggregator supports mixed pipeline (some tenants full-metering, some sampling). If tenant toggles back to full-metering, ensure historical sampled extrapolations are reconciled by running a catch-up job on retained raw traces for the month to produce invoices consistent with full-metering. Store sampling config and sampling seed per-tenant for reproducibility.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: sampling introduces billing variance affecting customer trust. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, opt-in default, visible dashboards, and grace adjustment for first billing cycle after opt-in.
Risk: deterministic sampling collides for high-traffic request_ids leading to biased samples. Mitigation: choose 128-bit hash and stratify by seq_len_class/kv_hit_pattern.

Risk: quota enforcement mismatch due to delayed aggregator. Mitigation: maintain synchronous conservative counters until aggregator confidence rises and use short lived windows for adaptive full-metering on anomalies.
